headline: 12 contracts catalogued across Ethereum L1 and L2; 9 LSP core contracts, 2 token receipt contracts, 1 governance token

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search surfaced mETH (0xd5f7838f...) and cmETH (0xe6829d9a...) token contracts on Ethereum L1
docs.mantle.xyz/meth contains deployment addresses table; deployed_contracts_doc set to Smart Contracts page
Audit links at docs.mantle.xyz/meth/security/audits reference Hexens, MixBytes, and other audit PDFs via GitHub raw links; audit era dates inferred as 2023-2024
GitHub mantle-lsp/contracts README.md contains definitive contract address table and role descriptions for all 9 L1 core contracts
Single chain (Ethereum L1); separate L2 deployment (mETH on Mantle L2) with different address recorded separately per role
No factory enumeration required; protocol does not use factory patterns for core contracts

Role taxonomy applied: token (mETH, cmETH, COOK), admin (Pauser, ProxyAdmin/Timelock), oracle (Oracle, OracleQuorumManager), other (ReturnsAggregator, ConsensusLayerReturnsReceiver, ExecutionLayerReturnsReceiver)
All addresses trace to ≥1 fetched URL in evidence[]; no snippet-only sightings in admin_addresses[]

rationale.verdict: Discovery walk completed: 9 Ethereum L1 core contracts (staking, token, oracle, returns aggregation, pause/receiver infrastructure) plus 2 receipt tokens (mETH, cmETH) plus 1 governance token (COOK) plus 1 L2 replica identified. Addresses sourced from canonical GitHub README, docs website, and block-explorer name-tag verification.

evidence.shows: README.md contract address table with 9 Ethereum L1 core contracts: Staking, METH, Oracle, OracleQuorumManager, UnstakeRequestsManager, Pauser, ReturnsAggregator, ConsensusLayerReturnsReceiver, ExecutionLayerReturnsReceiver, plus L2 METHL2 address

mETH token (0xd5f7838f5c461feff7fe49ea5ebaf7728bb0adfa) verified on Etherscan as 'Mantle: mETH Token' with TransparentUpgradeableProxy pattern; implementation at 0x052f52748109bae13d6319a463d64b6a2a613e52
cmETH token (0xe6829d9a7ee3040e1276fa75293bde931859e8fa) verified on Etherscan as 'Mantle: cmETH Token' with TransparentUpgradeableProxy pattern; described as '1:1 receipt token for mETH restaking'
UnstakeRequestsManager (0x38fDF7b489316e03eD8754ad339cb5c4483FDcf9) verified on Etherscan with label 'Mantle: Unstake Requests Manager'; holds 1297+ ETH and 1252+ mETH
Official website confirms mETH Protocol (liquid staking + restaking) with mETH and cmETH products; references institutional-grade liquid staking for Ethereum with ~24H redemption via Buffer Pool

Deployment addresses for Ethereum L1 including Staking, mETH Token, UnstakeRequestsManager, Oracle, OracleQuorumManager, ReturnsAggregator, ConsensusLayerReceiver, ExecutionLayerReceiver, Pauser, ProxyAdmin (Timelock), and L2 addresses; includes cmETH governance token address
COOK governance token address: 0x9F0C013016E8656bC256f948CD4B79ab25c7b94D on both Ethereum L1 and Mantle L2; confirms COOK is governance token for mETH Protocol
Audit references for Hexens (Aug 2023, Sep 2023), MixBytes, and other audit firms; audit URLs point to GitHub audit reports covering Liquid Staking Protocol, Oracle, and mETH security
Protocol uses OpenZeppelin TransparentUpgradableProxy with Timelock controller to add upgrade delay; ensures users can exit if they disagree with upgrades

protocol_metadata.about: mETH Protocol is an institutional-grade liquid staking and restaking platform on Ethereum L1 that allows users to stake ETH and receive mETH, a value-accumulating receipt token. The protocol includes cmETH, a restaking receipt token providing exposure to EigenLayer and other validated services. It features a liquidity buffer mechanism leveraging Aave markets for fast ~24-hour redemptions and is governed by the COOK token. The protocol is managed by the Mantle Ecosystem and audited by multiple security firms including Hexens and MixBytes.
